Identity.History: The Greek city-state of Athens is remembered as a famed center for the arts, learning, and philosophy, as well as one of the earliest forms of democracy. That wasn't to say that they weren't warriors. Athens, at its height, had one of the most powerful navies in the ancient world and, through conquering and colonizing, built a vast empire. The city-state rose to power after defeating the invading Achaemenid Persians twice in the early fifth century BC. Their empire lasted until 404 BC when they lost the Peloponnesian War to Sparta. While Athens never recovered its previous strength, the city-state kept its reputation as a place of learning, and its scholars were well sought out as teachers.
